basis: Skeletal and corneal disease 80-99%; valvular disease ~60-90%. Cap omits neurologic disease (30-79%), airway and hearing involvement.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: functionally significant valvular disease affects approximately 60-90% across the MPS I spectrum.
decisions.neurologic: none under cap: developmental impairment/regression occurs in 30-79%; more prevalent skeletal, ocular and cardiac damage takes priority.
decisions.ocular: involved: corneal opacity occurs in 80-99%; retinopathy and glaucoma occur in 30-79%, supporting functional eye involvement.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: dysostosis, joint stiffness and vertebral abnormalities occur in 80-99%; these are consequences of the metabolic disorder.

basis: Spinal nerve-root neurofibromas define disease (8/8). Pigment spots do not establish skin damage; cutaneous neurofibromas occur in only 1/5; Lisch nodules are non-damaging.

decisions.dermatologic: none: cafe-au-lait spots in 5/8 do not establish skin damage; cutaneous neurofibromas occur in only 1/5, and skin disease does not define this spinal subtype.

basis: Retroperitoneal smooth-muscle malignancy without a specified covered organ of origin; neither skeletal muscle nor locomotor connective tissue is established.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: retroperitoneal smooth muscle is outside the skeletal-muscle and locomotor-connective-tissue axis; a generic soft-tissue sarcoma parent does not establish that origin.

basis: Occlusive cerebral arteriopathy defines disease. Stroke may occur in >30% but is separately diagnosed; transient ischemic symptoms alone do not establish lasting brain damage.

decisions.neurologic: none: ischemic or hemorrhagic stroke may affect >30% but is a separately diagnosed complication; arterial occlusion and transient ischemic symptoms alone do not establish brain damage.

basis: Pontocerebellar hypoplasia, cerebral atrophy and developmental impairment define disease. Strabismus and blue sclerae in 1/1 do not establish direct ocular injury.

decisions.ocular: none: strabismus and blue sclerae were reported in 1/1, but neither establishes intrinsic eye damage or visual loss; strabismus can reflect neurologic dysfunction.

basis: Pituitary GH excess defines disease. Acral overgrowth (8/12) does not establish skeletal damage; skeletal abnormalities and visual-field defects are occasional; arthralgia 1/12.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: acral overgrowth occurs in 8/12, but skeletal disease is annotated as occasional (5-29%) and arthralgia occurs in 1/12; overgrowth alone does not establish locomotor damage.

basis: Porphyrin-metabolism disorder with defining neurovisceral attacks and motor neuropathy in the predominant monoallelic form; rare biallelic hemolysis does not generalize.

decisions.neurologic: primary: the definition explicitly characterizes the predominant monoallelic disease by neurovisceral attacks including motor neuropathy; incomplete penetrance does not negate a defining organ.

basis: Reactive fibro-osseous tissue forms in digital subcutis. Ectopic bone formation does not establish disease of native skeletal bone or locomotor connective tissue.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: the lesion arises in subcutaneous tissue; reactive ectopic ossification does not establish involvement of native bone, joints, tendons or skeletal muscle.

basis: Generalized lymphatic vascular dysplasia and intestinal lymphangiectasia (7/7); pulmonary lymphangiectasia 6/7 and pleural involvement 4/7. Developmental delay only 1/7.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: generalized lymphatic vascular malformation with lymphedema in 7/7 defines the syndrome; this label reflects lymphatic vessels rather than the uncommon cardiac defect.
decisions.dermatologic: none: lymphedema in 7/7 reflects lymphatic vascular dysfunction; independent skin injury or fibrosis is not established by the supplied evidence.

basis: Arterial and skin fragility characterize vascular EDS. Spontaneous intestinal rupture is a major diagnostic criterion despite ~15-25% frequency; joint laxity alone is insufficient.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: spontaneous intestinal rupture is a major diagnostic criterion for vascular EDS, qualifying despite its approximately 15-25% frequency.
decisions.dermatologic: primary: characteristic thin translucent skin, easy bruising and skin fragility are defining features of vascular EDS.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: small-joint hypermobility alone does not establish locomotor damage; this vascular subtype does not establish common destructive skeletal or joint disease.
